title: Pacing knobs latency & cost snapshot
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact working brief that captures a small set of microbenchmarks comparing different request/slot pacing knobs and their observable impact on latency percentiles and per-token cost. The goal is not to be exhaustive — it's a quick, reproducible sketch that product and runtime can iterate on.

Status & audience:
- Quick draft for internal review with runtime, platform, and devdocs.
- Intentionally terse: includes ASCII tables/plots for easy copy into decks.
- Not a canonical benchmark; please treat numbers as indicative (env: staging cluster, 8xA100-equivalent, mixed session mix).

Summary findings (high level):
- Small token-level pacing (100–200 tokens/sec per request) reduces tail latency p99 by ~12–18% for chat-like multi-turn sessions under medium burst; cost delta is negligible at sustained throughput but improves when prefix KV cache hits >40%.
- Coarse admission pacing (queueing at request ingress to limit concurrency) flattens p95–p99 spikes but increases median by 5–12ms; results in lower observed CPU/GPU context-switch churn and ~3–7% lower cost-per-1k-tokens at high spike rates.
- Aggressive batching windows (40–60ms) yield best amortized token cost but increase p90–p99 significantly for short responses (<50 tokens); useful for background/embedding workloads but dangerous for low-latency interactive features.

Experiment details (short):
- Workload mix: 60% interactive chat (mean 120 tokens per response, 1.6 turns/session), 30% short assistant replies (20–40 tokens), 10% background embeddings.
- Models: rwd-v1-medium (fp16), rwd-v1-small-quant (int8), open-compat-7b for a low-capacity comparison.
- Cluster: staging, 8-GPU pool (heterogeneous slice: 4xH100-lite + 4xA100-equivalent); tests routed to the same placement class.
- KV cache warm fraction: 45% unless otherwise noted.
- Measurement window: 20 minutes per config after a 2-minute warmup. 5 trial runs each.

Knobs evaluated (definitions):
- token_pace_cap: per-request token emission cap (tokens/sec). Values: off, 100, 200, 400.
- admission_window: short queue gating to cap inflight requests at X (slot count). Values: none, 32, 64.
- batching_window_ms: how long runtime holds a batch before dispatch. Values: 0, 20, 40, 60.
- prefetch_fraction: % of likely-followup prefix prefetched into KV cache (heuristic). Values: 0.0, 0.2, 0.5.

Primary metrics recorded (per run):
- p50_ms, p90_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms (end-to-end from request-agent to final token out).
- tokens_per_1k_cost_usd (estimated using spot GPU cost model used in platform pricing sim).
- KV_cache_hit_rate (observed, for correlation).
- GPU_util_peak (simple max sampled over window).

Representative results (ASCII tables). All numbers are medians across trials.

1) token_pace_cap sweep (admission_window=64, batching_window_ms=20)

| token_pace | p50_ms | p90_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | tokens/1k_cost ($) | kv_hit |
|------------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------------------|--------|
| off        | 78     | 220    | 330    | 620    | 0.86               | 0.45   |
| 100        | 83     | 190    | 275    | 520    | 0.88               | 0.45   |
| 200        | 89     | 175    | 255    | 510    | 0.90               | 0.45   |
| 400        | 95     | 168    | 252    | 508    | 0.92               | 0.45   |

Notes: token-level pacing shaved ~100ms off p99 vs uncapped in this mid-burst scenario; median shifted slightly up (small added emission delay). Cost per 1k tokens moved up slightly due to less batching efficiency but net platform-level cost didn't rise materially when KV hit remained stable.

2) admission_window sweep (token_pace=off, batching_window_ms=20)

| admission_slots | p50_ms | p90_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | tokens/1k_cost ($) | gpu_util_peak |
|-----------------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------------------|---------------|
| none            | 73     | 260    | 420    | 980    | 0.95               | 92%           |
| 32              | 79     | 210    | 300    | 560    | 0.91               | 85%           |
| 64              | 78     | 200    | 280    | 540    | 0.90               | 81%           |

Notes: Capping inflight work flattens the extreme tail and reduces peak GPU contention. Median slightly higher but acceptable for interactive flows if we keep p50 < 100ms. Cost improvement is visible because high tail-induced context switches and preemption are reduced.

3) batching_window tradeoffs (token_pace=200, admission_window=64)

| batching_ms | p50_ms | p90_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | tokens/1k_cost ($) | remark |
|-------------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------------------|--------|
| 0           | 86     | 210    | 260    | 510    | 0.98               | low amortization |
| 20          | 89     | 185    | 245    | 498    | 0.92               | good balance      |
| 40          | 95     | 225    | 330    | 640    | 0.80               | best cost, hurts tails for short responses |
| 60          | 110    | 310    | 420    | 900    | 0.72               | too high latency for interactive UX |

Simple ASCII sketch: p99 vs batching_ms (token_pace fixed at 200):

p99 (ms) 1000|           *
            800|         *   
            600|      *      
            400|   *         
            200| *           
             0+----------------
               0  20 40 60 (batching_ms)

Interpretation: if product needs sub-600ms p99 for short-turn chat, batching windows must be <=40ms and token_pace around 200 or lower; for background tasks where p99 isn't critical, 40–60ms yields significant cost reductions.

Correlation with KV cache:
- When KV hit >60% the cost benefit of pacing+larger batching compounds: amortized GPU compute per token drops because prefix decoding is skipped.
- If KV hit <30%, pacing hurts more (less prefix reuse => fewer tokens amortized => higher per-token compute).

Operational notes / gotchas observed in runs:
- Admission_window interacts subtly with autoscaler: if gate size is low and autoscaler threshold is conservative, we saw underprovisioning and increased latency during scaling events. Need to align gate with autoscaler warmup heuristics.
- Token_pace implementations that simply sleep between token emissions can confuse client-side streaming timeouts; recommend emitting frequent keepalive frames or a preliminary blank chunk to keep transports alive.
- Batching windows >40ms increase variance for collections of short requests (20–50 tokens) because they wait for the window to close; consider hybrid: immediate dispatch for short responses + delayed window for long responses.

Actionable recommendations (for product + runtime):
- Default: enable token_pace=200 with admission_window=64 and batching_window_ms=20 for mixed interactive workloads where p99 target is 600ms. Add feature flag to flip to aggressive-cost mode (batching=40–60, token_pace=off) for non-interactive pipelines.
- Expose token_pace and batching_window in the Console as a per-route suggestion with clear UI warning about p99 impact. Show expected delta derived from these sketches.
- Add telemetry to track client-side streaming timeouts when token_pace is active. If >0.5% of requests observe client disconnects, alert runtime team.

Next experiments (short backlog):
- Repeat the token_pace sweep with KV warm fraction toggled (20% vs 80%) to quantify compounding effects.
- Test hybrid immediate-for-short heuristic: classification by expected max_response_tokens at request admission. Measure p99 improvements on short-request-heavy traffic.
- Drive a cost model by extrapolating token/1k curves at steady-state across larger cluster shapes (24–128 GPUs) to understand trade-offs at scale.

Questions for reviewers:
- Is the UI/Console team comfortable exposing token_pace? Do we want it on by default as a suggested profile for new routes?
- Runtime: are there low-cost ways to implement token_pace without breaking streaming semantics (keepalive frame approach)?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Attach raw prometheus/exporter graphs and trial logs to CONFLUENCE-6932 (will upload after internal run verification).
- Sync with autoscaler owners about gate alignment (cc @Tom Alvarez).

References & links:
- JIRA-OPT-2211 (optimize backlog ticket for pacing knobs UI)
- slack:#optimize thread where Ethan ran the first micro-trial (2028-05-09)

End of snapshot.
